title: Topological sort
summary: Order tasks so every dependency comes first, using in-degrees (Kahn's algorithm).
hints: First compute `indeg[v]`: loop over every `u` and every `v` in `g[u]` and do `indeg[v]++`. The vertices with `indeg == 0` have no unmet dependencies; put all of them into a queue slice.
Repeatedly take `u` from the front of the queue, append it to `order`, and for each neighbour `v` decrement `indeg[v]`. When it reaches 0, `v` is ready: append it to the queue.

If the graph has a cycle, the vertices on it never reach in-degree 0, so `len(order) < len(g)` when the queue runs dry. Return nil in that case. `CanFinish` is then a short wrapper on the same idea - build a graph from the pairs (edge `b -> a` for each `{a, b}`) and check whether a full order exists.
